concepts.name: Weather versus climate
concepts.summary: Explain that weather is short-term atmospheric conditions while climate is the long-term statistical pattern over decades.

concepts.name: Components of climate system
concepts.summary: Name the atmosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere, lithosphere and biosphere and state that they interact to shape climate.

concepts.name: Solar radiation as energy source
concepts.summary: Explain that the Sun supplies nearly all of Earth's climate energy and that latitude causes uneven heating.

concepts.name: Natural greenhouse effect
concepts.summary: Describe how greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, keeping Earth's surface warmer than it would otherwise be.

concepts.name: Major greenhouse gases
concepts.summary: Identify water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and their main natural and human sources.

concepts.name: Fossil fuel emissions
concepts.summary: Explain that burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide and is the main driver of recent warming.

concepts.name: Observed global warming
concepts.summary: State that global average surface temperature has risen by roughly 1.1 °C since the late 1800s.

misconceptions.text: A single cold winter or snowstorm disproves global warming.
The greenhouse effect is itself harmful and would not exist without human activity.
The ozone hole is the main cause of global warming.

concepts.name: Earth's energy balance
concepts.summary: Apply the idea that incoming absorbed sunlight equals outgoing infrared at equilibrium to reason about warming or cooling.

concepts.name: Albedo and reflectivity
concepts.summary: Use albedo values of ice, ocean, forest and clouds to predict how surface changes alter absorbed sunlight.

concepts.name: Carbon cycle reservoirs and fluxes
concepts.summary: Trace carbon among atmosphere, oceans, biosphere, soils and rocks and distinguish fast from slow exchanges.

concepts.name: Ocean heat and circulation
concepts.summary: Explain how oceans absorb most excess heat and redistribute it through currents.

concepts.name: Instrumental temperature record
concepts.summary: Read a temperature anomaly graph relative to a baseline and describe the long-term trend despite year-to-year variability.

concepts.name: Ice cores and proxy records
concepts.summary: Explain how ice cores, tree rings and sediments record past temperature and atmospheric composition.

concepts.name: Ocean acidification
concepts.summary: Apply carbonate chemistry to explain how dissolved CO2 lowers ocean pH and harms shell-forming organisms.

concepts.name: Sea level rise drivers
concepts.summary: Distinguish thermal expansion, land-ice melt and sea-ice melt as contributors to sea level change.

misconceptions.text: Melting sea ice raises sea level in the same way as melting land ice.
Ocean acidification means the ocean has become acidic with pH below 7.
Plants and oceans will absorb all the extra CO2 so atmospheric levels cannot keep rising.

concepts.name: Radiative forcing
concepts.summary: Quantify and compare forcings in W/m² from greenhouse gases, aerosols and solar changes.

concepts.name: Climate feedback mechanisms
concepts.summary: Analyse water vapour, ice-albedo, cloud and lapse-rate feedbacks and whether each amplifies or damps warming.

concepts.name: Climate sensitivity
concepts.summary: Interpret equilibrium and transient sensitivity as the warming response to doubled CO2 and its uncertainty range.

concepts.name: Attribution of recent warming
concepts.summary: Use fingerprints such as stratospheric cooling and hemispheric patterns to show that human activity, not natural causes, drives warming.

concepts.name: Milankovitch orbital cycles
concepts.summary: Explain how orbital variations pace glacial and interglacial cycles and why they cannot explain current warming.

concepts.name: Aerosols and volcanic effects
concepts.summary: Analyse how sulfate aerosols reflect sunlight and mask part of greenhouse warming.

concepts.name: Climate modelling basics
concepts.summary: Describe how models discretise physics on grids, are validated by hindcasts, and project scenarios.

concepts.name: Emissions scenarios and pathways
concepts.summary: Relate scenarios of emissions and socioeconomic development to projected concentration and temperature outcomes.

misconceptions.text: Past natural climate change shows that current warming must also be natural.
Climate models are just extrapolations of past trends rather than physics-based simulations.
Water vapour is the main cause of warming, so CO2 does not matter.

concepts.name: Tipping points and abrupt change
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence and thresholds for ice sheet collapse, AMOC weakening, permafrost and Amazon dieback.

concepts.name: Carbon cycle feedbacks
concepts.summary: Analyse how warming alters natural sinks and releases carbon, changing airborne fraction.

concepts.name: Carbon budget and cumulative emissions
concepts.summary: Analyse the near-linear relationship between cumulative CO2 emissions and warming to derive budgets for temperature targets.

concepts.name: Extreme event attribution
concepts.summary: Evaluate how studies estimate changes in the likelihood and intensity of heatwaves, floods and storms due to warming.

concepts.name: Regional climate projections and downscaling
concepts.summary: Analyse how precipitation, monsoon and drought changes differ regionally and the uncertainty in regional projections.

concepts.name: Paleoclimate analogues
concepts.summary: Evaluate how past warm and cold periods constrain sensitivity and show rates and impacts of change.

concepts.name: Uncertainty and model ensembles
concepts.summary: Evaluate sources of projection uncertainty (scenario, model, internal variability) and how ensembles represent them.

concepts.name: Mitigation and carbon removal pathways
concepts.summary: Evaluate how emission pathways, net zero and carbon dioxide removal relate to temperature outcomes.

misconceptions.text: Warming will stop soon after emissions fall to zero-growth levels, so cutting emission growth is enough.
Uncertainty in projections means scientists do not know whether serious impacts will occur.
Attribution studies claim a single extreme event was caused solely by climate change.

concepts.name: Cloud feedback uncertainty
concepts.summary: Evaluate why cloud responses dominate sensitivity spread and which observations and process studies could reduce it.

concepts.name: Constraining sensitivity with multiple evidence
concepts.summary: Critically combine process understanding, historical and paleo evidence and emergent constraints to judge sensitivity estimates.

concepts.name: Pattern effects and ocean variability
concepts.summary: Assess how evolving ocean warming patterns and decadal variability influence feedbacks and the interpretation of trends.

concepts.name: Design of climate experiments
concepts.summary: Design model or observational experiments that isolate forcings, feedbacks or variability to test a specific hypothesis.

concepts.name: Solar and aerosol geoengineering assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate the physical effects, risks and termination hazards of proposed climate interventions.

concepts.name: Integrated climate risk assessment
concepts.summary: Synthesise hazard, exposure, vulnerability and uncertainty to build a risk assessment for a region or sector.

concepts.name: Evaluation of climate evidence claims
concepts.summary: Appraise datasets, methods and claims, including homogenisation and contrarian arguments, against the weight of evidence.

misconceptions.text: Cloud feedbacks are so uncertain that sensitivity is essentially unconstrained.
Geoengineering by reflecting sunlight would fully offset the effects of CO2 including ocean acidification.
A pause or slowdown in surface warming over a decade disproves the long-term forced trend.
